speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help you with your acute diarrhea, can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if there has been any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-associated colitis (likely *C. difficile* infection). Given the history of recent levofloxacin use and acute watery diarrhea with cramping, this clinical picture is highly suggestive. I will proceed with requesting stool studies to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Stool_C_diff_toxin_PCR. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Ova_and_Parasites.
